endpoint.description: The URL of the Web API endpoint to be called.

method.description: The HTTP method to be used for the API call.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested or submitted.

params.description: Query parameters to be appended to the endpoint URL.

body.description: The JSON payload to be sent with POST, PUT, or PATCH requests.

data.description: The actual data to be sent in the request body.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for a server response before timing out. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find a 3 bedroom apartment in Zurich. We need to use the web API to search for apartments. The function signature: make_webapi_call with endpoint, method, headers, params, body, timeout.

We need to construct a GET request to an endpoint that can search for apartments. The user didn't specify a particular API. We need to guess a suitable endpoint. Possibly "https://api.example.com/apartments/search". But we don't know the actual endpoint. We might need to ask clarifying question? The instruction says we should not ask clarifying questions unless necessary. But we need to provide a function call. We could assume a generic endpoint like "https://api.realestate.com/search". But we need to provide something plausible.

We can use "https://api.realestate.com/apartments/search" with query parameters: city=Zurich, bedrooms=3. Let's do that. Use GET method. Provide headers: Content-Type: application/json. No body needed. Timeout default.

Thus call:

{
  endpoint: "https://api.realestate.com/apartments/search",
  method: "GET",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  params: { city: "Zurich", bedrooms: "3" }
}

But the function signature expects params: { query?: string }. That seems limited. But we can pass query string like "city=Zurich&bedrooms=3". But the param structure only has query optional. So maybe we need to put the entire query string into query param. So query: "city=Zurich&bedrooms=3". That might be acceptable.

Alternatively, we can use body with data: JSON string. But GET doesn't have body.

Given the function signature, we can set params: { query: "city=Zurich&bedrooms=3" }.

Let's do that.
